candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
candidates.summary: Open to trout fishing all year — Prosser Creek Reservoir is not on CCR §7.50(b)'s special-regulations list, so the statewide default for lakes and reservoirs applies (no closed season).

candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
candidates.summary: 5 trout per day, 10 in possession — the statewide default limit for California lakes and reservoirs (rainbow, brown, golden, and cutthroat trout combined). Note: Prosser Creek itself (the stream below the dam) has a separate 0-trout/artificial-lures-barbless special regulation (7.50(b)(113)) — that does not apply to the reservoir.

candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
candidates.summary: 5 kokanee salmon per day, 10 in possession — Prosser Creek Reservoir is not among the reduced-limit exception waters (Bucks, Pardee, New Bullards Bar, Trinity), so the statewide landlocked-salmon default applies. Counted separately from the trout limit.

candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
candidates.summary: 5 black bass per day — statewide default for California lakes and reservoirs. Smallmouth bass is a well-documented resident species at Prosser Creek Reservoir.

candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
candidates.summary: 12-inch total-length minimum for black bass — statewide default for lakes and reservoirs.

candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife
candidates.summary: Anglers 16 and older must carry a valid California sport fishing license.

candidates.authorityName: California Department of Fish and Wildlife

parameters.requires_permit_note: A valid second-rod stamp is required to fish with a second rod.

candidates.summary: No bait or lure restrictions. Anglers may fish with up to 2 rods at once if they hold a valid second-rod stamp.
